samples: This module reads a JSON configuration file into a validated settings record (a port from 1 to 65535, 1 to 64 workers, and a log level of Quiet, Normal or Verbose). It reports a failure that distinguishes an unreadable file from content that doesn't match the expected shape or limits. It also provides built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, Normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply when loading fails. The older default-fallback loader is deprecated in favor of that one, and the only access it needs is read access to the filesystem.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks it against a fixed shape: a port from 1 to 65535, a worker count from 1 to 64, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, it reports which of those two problems occurred. It also offers built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply, while the older fallback-to-defaults loader is deprecated in favor of that one.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks it against the expected shape: a port between 1 and 65535, 1 to 64 workers, and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file can't be read or doesn't match, loading fails with an error that says which problem occurred. It also offers built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a loader that falls back to a configuration you supply, which replaces an older, now-deprecated fallback function that used the built-in defaults.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks that it has a valid port (1 to 65535), a worker count (1 to 64) and a log level of quiet, normal or verbose. If the file cannot be read or does not match that shape, it reports a distinct error saying which problem occurred. It also provides built-in defaults (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a fallback loader that lets you supply your own configuration to use when loading fails. The older default-based loader is deprecated in favor of that fallback loader.

This module reads a JSON configuration file for a service and checks that it has a valid port (1–65535), a worker count (1–64) and a log level (quiet, normal or verbose). If the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape, it reports a specific error. It also supplies a built-in default configuration (port 8080, 4 workers, normal logging) and a function that falls back to a configuration you choose when loading fails; the older fallback function is deprecated in favor of that one.
